title: Singapore forms task force to strengthen defences against AI-enabled cyber threats
key_facts: Singapore has formed a task force of more than 20 experts and industry leaders to strengthen the infocomm and media sector's defences against AI-enabled and AI-accelerated cyber threats.

The Frontier AI Resilience and Security Taskforce (FAIRS) brings together leaders from telecoms, media, cybersecurity and AI, the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) said on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026.
It is expected to publish a report with practical guidelines and best practices in the first half of 2027.
IMDA chief executive Ng Cher Pong said some risks cannot be managed by testing individual AI applications alone.
The task force will examine how networks and systems can be strengthened and segmented so vulnerabilities do not cause widespread disruption, and how network visibility and response can keep pace.
The announcement came a day after Singapore launched a new national cybersecurity strategy aimed at earlier and faster responses to AI-enabled threats.
CNA links the launch to this year's incidents in which AI agents went "rogue", including hundreds of OpenAI agents that hacked Hugging Face.
